patch_description:
The current program spends most of its 1.2s budget inside `linprog` because the LP is built with Python loops appending dense rows ((4n+m) x n dense matrix, ~325x26 built elementwise) — this is called once per hill-climb step, so only a few hundred moves get evaluated. Two targeted changes:

1. Vectorize the LP construction with numpy index arrays and `scipy.sparse.csr_matrix` (triu_indices for pairs), cutting per-solve cost several-fold so many more moves fit in the same time. Also cache pairwise distances across steps (only one center changes per step) — but the simplest safe win is the vectorized sparse build, which prior Gen-1 showed works and is fast.

2. Use the freed headroom: extend the deadline to ~2.4s (eval_time was 1.76 with a 1.2s deadline, so ~2.5s total is safe), and run a cheap 3-start scheme: the two best base layouts, each with ±0.005 jitter, annealed briefly, then spend remaining time refining the winner. Cheap variants of a strong base (per the Gen-8 lesson) rather than diverse layouts.
